title: rtmpt: limit the number of iterations in rtmpt_get_amf_length().
description:
This prevents a infinite-loop caused by crafted packets.

Fix: #17813.

notes.body: assigned to @crondaemon
I'm not sure that returning 0 here is a good idea because we could get stuck in the next while loop - for example, `rtmpt_get_amf_param`
What do you suggest?
I could return -1 and check this value in the caller.
I think we should stop dissecting the packet if it reaches here. It's malformed anyway so the parsing should not continue IMHO
I'm pushing a new version. Let me know what you think.
I'm keeping returning 0, but I'm checking it in the caller, that propagates the error.
looks good to me

Shouldn't this check if `(--iterations == 0)` instead of erring out the first time the check is hit?

!13933
if we get `itemlen = 0` here this loop could continue for a very long time / forever
itemlen should be defined as `guint32` (it's a DWORD)
Ok. But rv has to be changed as well.
